paragraphs: R' Shimon son of R' Yose. In Pesahim 118b, when R' Shimon son of R' Yose became ill [the checked Bavli reads Yishmael son of Yose], Rabbi sent to him, “Tell us two or three things that you said in your father's name.” Ein Yaakov's reading is R' Yishmael son of R' Yose; see his entry. There: R' Shimon son of Rabbi—some say R' Shimon son of R' Yose [the checked Bavli gives Yishmael son of Yose in this alternative]—said to Rabbi, “To whom do these refer?” In Nedarim 66b [the checked Bavli also reads Yishmael son of Yose], someone said to his wife, “You are forbidden by a konam to benefit from me until you show R' Shimon son of R' Yose a beautiful feature in yourself.” In Ran there: R' Yishmael son of R' Yose. R' Shimon son of R' Yose: Yalkut, end of Pekudei. In Hullin 5, beginning of side b: R' Shimon son of R' Yose in R' Shimon's name. There, 124a [the checked Bavli has Rav Huna report in Yishmael son of Yose’s name]: Rav Huna said in R' Shimon son of R' Yose's name. In Shabbat 81a: R' Shimon son of R' Yose in his father's name. Perhaps these R' Shimon son of R' Yose notices refer to the son of R' Yose ben Lakunya mentioned above. One should not suppose that R' Yose is ben Halafta, for R' Yose bar Halafta had no son Shimon.
